newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse July turnover 228.9 pct up mo/mo.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse July turnover 228.9 pct up mo/mo.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange reported on Thursday a 228.9 percent increase in its July turnover compared with June mainly due to heavy trade in central bank short-term bonds on the Podgorica-based bourse.
Total July turnover rose to 124.98 million dinars ($20.43 million) in 230 transactions from 54.59 million dinars in 165 deals in June, the bourse said in its monthly report.
Short-term securities accounted for 84.57 percent of the July total.
The bourse reported 70 million dinars worth of deals in central bank short-term bonds.

In July alone, the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) auctioned in Podgorica two 30 million dinar-tranches of 20- and 30-day bonds carrying a 41.63 percent annual interest. Both tranches were entirely sold, the report said.
Another 10 million dinars of NBY 10-day bonds, carrying an annual 61.15 percent interest, were traded on the secondary market.
Commercial paper accounted for 34.23 million dinars, while 1.46 million dinars was in bills issued by the Montenegrin Commodity Reserve Agency.
Giro money deals, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, accounted for the remaining 19.29 million dinars. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
